1.finding: Two bonus issues before filing: 2:1 on 28-Jul-2025 and 1:1 on 8-May-2026 (pp. 93-94); EPS restated post-bonus for all periods. FY26 basic EPS Rs 10.36 on PAT to owners Rs 21.82 cr = 2.106 crore weighted shares; pre-offer capital is 2.2855 crore shares (p. 92), on which FY26 EPS is Rs 9.55. Private placement of 11,38,898 shares at Rs 180 in Jan-2026 = Rs 90 after the 1:1 bonus.

2.finding: CFO Rs 2.03 / 18.39 / 3.30 cr FY24-26 against PAT Rs 4.81 / 20.03 / 22.33 cr: cumulative CFO 50% of PAT. FY26 CFO was held down by an inventory build of Rs 20.34 cr for the new tube and 2/3-wheeler tyre plants and Rs 6.52 cr of other financial assets (including related-party loans). Q1 FY27 CFO Rs 6.25 cr against PAT Rs 6.42 cr.

3.finding: Current tax Rs 1.84 / 6.06 / 6.61 cr = 29% / 21% / 21% of PBT; deferred tax rises because tax depreciation (Rs 8.68 cr FY26) far exceeds book depreciation (Rs 0.45 cr) (p. 332). Tax paid Rs 1.30 / 3.86 / 5.87 cr (p. 71).

4.finding: Loans and advances to promoters and promoter entities outstanding Rs 13.13 cr at Jun-26 (Mohit Gupta Rs 5.81 cr, Manju Gupta Rs 1.94 cr, Moonriver Interiors LLP Rs 2.63 cr, Qualimax Electronics Rs 1.11 cr and others), given without repayment terms and interest-free except to the two promoters (p. 82); FY26 gross loans to Moonriver Interiors Rs 9.73 cr and to Mohit Gupta Rs 7.52 cr. Disclosed in full; no issue proceeds go to promoters (p. 115). No related-party capex.

5.finding: Fresh issue is a fixed 57,61,831 shares; specific objects Rs 72.49 cr (debt Rs 45.00 cr, rubber recycling plant Rs 19.06 cr, solid tyre plant Rs 8.44 cr). Grossed up for assumed 8% expenses and GCP the objects need about Rs 172 a share: the cap funds the objects with GCP at about 19% of the fresh issue (cap 25%).

6.finding: No revaluation of property, plant and equipment in any year.

7.finding: Goodwill Rs 6.47 cr from the MG Industries acquisition (5.1% of equity); PPE fair-value uplift Rs 9.58 cr on acquisition (p. 313).

8.finding: JK Tyre & Industries 36.25% / 41.19% / 59.56% of revenue FY24-26 and 88.67% in Q1 FY27; the second customer fell from 48.69% (FY25) and 25.15% (FY26) to 5.63% in Q1 FY27; top 10 customers 96-99%. Top supplier 31.74% of FY26 purchases; top 10 suppliers 73.69%. A long-term agreement exists only with JK Tyre (p. 23).

9.finding: Contingent liabilities Rs 6.63 cr at Jun-26 (5.0% of equity): Jain Enterprises' Rs 4.19 cr recovery suit (Delhi High Court, in mediation) and GST/VAT demands Rs 2.44 cr. Materiality threshold Rs 0.79 cr (5% of average PAT). No criminal or regulatory action against the company or promoters.

R1.finding: Statutory and peer-review auditor G B S G & Associates; no qualified opinion or disclaimer on internal financial controls for FY24-Q1 FY27 (p. 54). The FY26 change from WDV to straight-line depreciation is disclosed (p. 313) and is treated in the earnings-quality test.

R2.finding: The accounting software used in FY26 did not have an audit-trail (edit log) feature; party balances are subject to confirmation (p. 352). Delays of up to 90-100 days in GST annual returns and up to 91 days in EPF compliances (p. 35).

R4.finding: Reg 6(1): operating profit (PBT + finance cost - other income) Rs 8.73 / 27.80 / 34.61 cr FY24-26, average Rs 23.7 cr above the Rs 15 cr test (our computation); net worth positive each year.

R6.finding: Sarthi Capital Advisors: small Mumbai lead manager; track record not compiled in this run.

rationale.g1: Revenue from operations Rs 90.11 / 101.32 / 129.76 cr FY24-26 (+12.4%, +28.1%, the FY25-26 rise partly from consolidating MG Industries from Nov-2024) and Rs 47.74 cr in Q1 FY27 (p. 70), as the new Dehradun tube plant (Dec-2025) and Gwalior 2/3-wheeler tyre plant (Dec-2025; 37-39% utilised) ramp up (p. 134). Not annualised. Neutral 25% in Y1 fading to 9%; Bear 8% fading to 5% (JK Tyre volumes flat, second customer lost); Bull 35% fading to 11% (new plants and IPO-funded recycling and solid-tyre lines fill).
rationale.m: EBITDA (issuer KPI, excludes other income) 11.52% / 30.49% / 27.02% FY24-26 and 22.43% in Q1 FY27 (p. 131). The FY25 step-up came from buying premixed compound and lower rubber prices (pp. 378, 381). Neutral 23% (three-year average 23.0%, close to the latest quarter); Bear 17%; Bull 27% (FY26 level).
rationale.nwc: Inventory + receivables - payables = 24.9% / 47.4% / 47.2% of revenue FY24-26 (pp. 68-69); Q1 FY27 Rs 61.66 cr. Neutral 40% (three-year average 39.8%); Bear 47% (FY25-26 level); Bull 32%.
rationale.roic: ROCE (issuer) 9.65% / 18.22% / 15.41% FY24-26 (p. 131). Terminal ROIC 15% (Neutral), 11% Bear, 18% Bull.
rationale.capex: FY26 depreciation (Rs 0.45 cr) is not a normal charge: the switch from WDV to straight-line, with excess past depreciation set off, cut it by Rs 3.30 cr (p. 313), and tax depreciation was Rs 8.68 cr (p. 332). D&A for the DCF is set at Rs 8.0 cr, straight-line on the Jun-26 gross block (plant Rs 107.28 cr over 15 years = Rs 7.15 cr; buildings Rs 27.13 cr over 30 years = Rs 0.90 cr) (p. 313). FY26 capex of Rs 30.66 cr (p. 71) was the one-off build of the new tube and 2/3-wheeler plants. Existing capacity - tyre flaps 43.2 lakh, tubes 27.6 lakh and 2/3-wheeler tyres 7.1 lakh units a year, run at 79%, 84% and 37% in FY26 (p. 134) - supports roughly Rs 195-200 cr of revenue at FY26 realisations (our estimate from pp. 134, 378) against Rs 130 cr in FY26, so organic capex is taken as maintenance (= D&A) plus 0.10 x revenue growth (Rs 10.84 cr on FY26). IPO-funded capex Rs 27.49 cr (recycling and solid tyres, p. 114) is added in Neutral and Bull. Net debt Rs 103.86 cr = long-term borrowings Rs 51.23 cr + short-term Rs 57.68 cr + leases Rs 0.63 cr - cash Rs 5.68 cr (Mar-26, pp. 68-69); related-party loans of Rs 11.35 cr are not treated as cash. Fresh issue fixed at 57,61,831 shares = Rs 99.10 cr at the cap; expenses assumed 8%. PAT for the relative value is FY26 PAT to owners adjusted for the depreciation-method change and balances written back: Rs 21.82 cr - Rs 3.64 cr = Rs 18.18 cr (earnings-quality test).

adjustments.item: Depreciation cut by the switch from WDV to straight-line (excess past depreciation set off)
adjustments.reason: The holding company (FY26) and MG Industries (FY25) moved from WDV to straight-line and set the excess of past WDV depreciation against the new charge, so some asset classes bore no depreciation: FY26 depreciation fell to Rs 0.45 cr on a Rs 136.9 cr gross block, lower by Rs 2.45 cr (company) + Rs 0.85 cr (MG Industries); FY25 lower by Rs 1.28 cr. Tax depreciation was Rs 8.68 cr in FY26 (p. 332). Q1 FY27 is lower by a further Rs 1.95 cr; only Rs 0.92 cr of excess remains to absorb, so the charge rises to a normal level in FY27.
